Topics · Who was Muhammad?

Did the Arabs know the Quran's stories before?

The Quran says one thing about Noah's account, its opponents another, and the book keeps both, side by side.

Part 1 of 3

﴿تِلْكَ مِنْ أَنۢبَآءِ ٱلْغَيْبِ نُوحِيهَآ إِلَيْكَ ۖ مَا كُنتَ تَعْلَمُهَآ أَنتَ وَلَا قَوْمُكَ مِن قَبْلِ هَـٰذَا ۖ فَٱصْبِرْ ۖ إِنَّ ٱلْعَـٰقِبَةَ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you, [O Muḥammad]. You knew it not, neither you nor your people, before this. So be patient; indeed, the [best] outcome is for the righteous.

Quran · Hud 11:49

The verse closes the account of Noah with a sentence to the Prophet: neither you nor your people knew this before. Notice first its limits. It speaks of this account as told here, and not of every name Arabs had heard. Notice second where it was said: it was recited before the very people it describes. Had they known this account in this form, they could have said so. It is a public claim, and that makes their reply worth reading.

A question for you

If the sentence were false, what would you expect them to say?

If you sayWe know all this already.
ThenThat is the reply the next part looks for, and it finds something close to it.
If you sayNothing. They would ignore it.
ThenPerhaps. Yet the Quran records that they answered, and the next part gives their words.

Part 2 of 3

﴿وَقَالُوٓا۟ أَسَـٰطِيرُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ ٱكْتَتَبَهَا فَهِىَ تُمْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِ بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

And they say, "Legends of the former peoples which he has written down, and they are dictated to him morning and afternoon."

Quran · Al-Furqan 25:5

﴿وَإِذَا تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَايَـٰتُنَا قَالُوا۟ قَدْ سَمِعْنَا لَوْ نَشَآءُ لَقُلْنَا مِثْلَ هَـٰذَآ ۙ إِنْ هَـٰذَآ إِلَّآ أَسَـٰطِيرُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And when Our verses are recited to them, they say, "We have heard. If we willed, we could say [something] like this. This is not but legends of the former peoples."

Quran · Al-Anfal 8:31

Here is what they said, and the Quran keeps it: tales of the ancients. We have heard this, and we could say the like if we wished. This is serious, and it cuts both ways. It suggests some of this sounded familiar, at least in outline. It also shows something else: they add that someone dictates it to him, so they did not see it as what he had always said. The Quran leaves both sentences on the record, its own and theirs, for you to set side by side.

A question for you

What do you think best fits both sentences together?

If you sayThey knew the names, and not the tellings.
ThenThat holds the two sentences together, and the next part gives the Quran's own word for that difference.
If you sayThey knew the stories well.
ThenThen a question remains: why was the charge that someone was teaching him? That has its own Step.
If you sayI cannot tell from this.
ThenAn honest answer, since the record cannot measure what people held in their minds. Read on for what the Quran says of it.

Part 3 of 3

﴿أَن تَقُولُوٓا۟ إِنَّمَآ أُنزِلَ ٱلْكِتَـٰبُ عَلَىٰ طَآئِفَتَيْنِ مِن قَبْلِنَا وَإِن كُنَّا عَن دِرَاسَتِهِمْ لَغَـٰفِلِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

[We revealed it] lest you say, "The Scripture was only sent down to two groups before us, but we were of their study unaware,"

Quran · Al-An'am 6:156

Another verse gives the missing distinction. It imagines his people saying: the Book was sent to two groups before us, and we were unaware of their study. Knowing that your neighbours have a book is one thing. Knowing what is in it is another. Many people today know the name of a holy book they have never opened. The Quran places his people there: aware that others had scripture, unaware of its study. This describes the depth of what they held, and it fits both earlier verses.

A question for you

How much hearing would be enough to explain what he brought?

If you sayA few names would be enough.
ThenThen compare a few names with the telling of a whole chapter, such as Joseph. Then weigh.
If you sayLong hearing, from someone who knew.
ThenThen the question is that source. The Quran's reply is that the man they pointed to spoke a foreign tongue (16:103). See the Step on the teacher.
If you sayHis life among them holds the answer.
ThenThat is what 10:16 appeals to, and it has its own Step.

Your reflection

What had you heard of all your life, and only truly knew once you read it for yourself?
